_comment: Sensitive-content carve-out for the AR/MS translation pipeline (CR083). Generalizes DEF094. Two policies: 'exclude' = held to EN, pre-seeded, routed to Saiful/external, never sent to the LLM. 'strict_review' = auto-translated normally but requires the stricter Tier-3 confidence bar (>=3 distinct models, zero issues of any severity, not just critical) before counting as verified. Everything else in these files gets ordinary treatment.

exclude.reason: CR069 Phase 1b — each key's own @description already says 'Saiful arranges translation externally' and carries load-bearing translator notes (e.g. 'unscreened' must never become 'haram'). Pre-seed app_ar.arb/app_ms.arb with the literal EN value so translate_arb_lan.py's skip-unless-overwrite logic leaves them alone.

All 15 entries are dedicated Sharia-ruling Q&A (fiqh-adjacent explanatory content, not app-mechanics description). Relocate out of content/ai_coach/ for the duration of any translate_content_lan.py --type ai_coach run; restore after.

strict_review.reason: Saiful, 2026-07-24: auto-translate this 10-lesson Islamic-finance unit like the rest of Tier 3, but require a stricter confidence bar than ordinary lessons given CR069's own translator notes flag this content class as highest mistranslation risk.

Only entry in this file that explains the halal screen's ruling substance (AAOIFI screens, 'confirm with your own scholar'). The other 39 entries (incl. qa_plt_mandate_fields, qa_plt_coach_cant_customize) merely name 'halal' as one Mandate toggle among several — ordinary treatment.
All 10/10 challenges for this month are Islamic-finance-themed (riba, sukuk, AAOIFI ratio screens, purification). Same policy as the lesson unit.

20 terms tagged islamic_finance. Definitional (not exegetical) but include Arabic-loanword proper terms that must be transliterated, not translated (see style_guide_ar_ms.md) — same stricter bar applies.
